claim: Challenger Deep maximum depth measured by NOAA/UNH multibeam bathymetry
excerpt: The absolute deepest point within the Challenger Deep western basin was determined to be 10,984 ± 25 meters (36,037 ft) at 95% confidence level.
human_anchor: 2,136 meters deeper than Mount Everest is tall if inverted into the ocean

claim: Challenger Deep depth in feet
excerpt: Depth measured between 36,037 ft and 36,070 ft across multibeam sounding grids.
human_anchor: The cruising altitude of a commercial Boeing 777 passenger airliner pointed straight down

claim: Hydrostatic pressure at the floor of the Challenger Deep
excerpt: At the floor of the Challenger Deep (~10,994 m), ambient pressure reaches approximately 1,086 to 1,100 bar (over 15,750 to 16,000 psi).
human_anchor: Equivalent to an adult African elephant balanced on the surface of a human postage stamp

claim: Date of first manned descent by US Navy Bathyscaphe Trieste

human_anchor: 9 years before Apollo 11 touched down on the Moon

claim: Descent duration of Bathyscaphe Trieste
excerpt: The descent took 4 hours and 47 minutes under a surface water temperature of 84°F and seafloor temperature of 37.4°F.
human_anchor: Nearly the runtime of two full feature-length films in pitch blackness

claim: Trieste steel pressure sphere wall thickness
excerpt: The 5-inch thick Krupp forged steel sphere remained structurally intact.
human_anchor: Thicker than the frontal armor plate of a World War II Sherman tank

claim: NOAA PMEL deployed titanium-encased hydrophone to Challenger Deep

human_anchor: Midsummer 2015 deployment by Coast Guard Cutter Sequoia

claim: Continuous recording duration of NOAA hadal hydrophone
excerpt: The instrument recorded ambient sound continuously for 23 days at a sampling rate of 32 kHz.

claim: Descent speed of titanium hydrophone through water column

claim: Sampling rate of NOAA Challenger Deep hydrophone
excerpt: The instrument recorded ambient sound continuously for 23 days at a sampling rate of 32 kHz (16-bit resolution).

claim: Duration of the Western Pacific Biotwang acoustic signal

claim: Peak high-frequency metallic sweep of Western Pacific Biotwang
